data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old English word ‘ingas’, meaning ‘people’ or ‘tribe’. The suffix ‘-les’ was added to denote a stranger or foreigner. In medieval England, the name Ingles was often given to children born to English mothers and foreign fathers, or vice versa. The name Ingles carries the meaning “English stranger, foreigner” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin.
